The morula is an aggregate of nuclei surrounded by an extracellular matrix, in which the cytoplasm is separated from the nuclei by narrow cytoplasmic strands.

Two large nuclei in each of these cells provide the first evidence for division of a single cell that has been involved in the formation of all germ layers. This phase of development is known as the morula stage and represents a major event during the early development of the embryo.
A large number of such morulas are isolated from the eggs and cultured in a test tube for four days, during which time they become fully blastocysts.
